_readme: Coverage map for arXiv:1902.08184v4 -- 'Stability conditions in families',
Bayer, Lahoz, Macri, Nuer, Perry, Stellari. Created for destination issue
#198 under epic #190 (stability-families).
THIS IS NOT A TRUST RECORD AND NOT A MINT SURFACE. It is a zero-claim map
of the paper's structure onto statuses. formalization.yaml's `source`
remains the Bridgeland 2007 record, and registry/bridgeland2007.json
remains the only mint surface; nothing in this file changes either, and
nothing in this file may be cited as theorem coverage. The only status
that ever counts as coverage is 'formalized'. A 'mapped' entry remains a
candidate correspondence and makes no coverage claim.
Validation: python scripts/check_coverage_map.py
Run it before and after every edit to this file. It fails on any status
outside the vocabulary, any non-target status without complete evidence,
and any corpus-derived identifier key.
Update ownership: the owner (Chris Dare) promotes statuses; agents may
propose a promotion only by PR carrying the evidence fields the validator
demands, and 'formalized' additionally requires explicit owner acceptance
recorded in the entry. Adding sections, fixing titles against the pinned
PDF, and adding tracking links are ordinary edits; status promotion is
not.
Quotes: none are minted here. When a quote is later needed it must be
checked directly against the v4 artifact identified in `source` -- never
against the arXMCP corpus, whose rows carry no arXiv version (see
`corpus_note`).

corpus_note.mint_rule: No durable key in this repository may be derived from a chunk ID or a notebook slug. This file contains neither, and the validator fails if either kind of key is added. Rationale: chunk IDs are sha256(NFC(body_text))[:16] over corpus bytes of an UNVERSIONED fetch, so they are neither stable across corpus rebuilds nor attributable to v4.

near_term_coordinates.note: Weak stability conditions and HRS tilting. The repository holds abstract HRS-tilt machinery and source-facing candidates for Definitions 14.1--14.12, display (14.1), Proposition 14.16, and Lemma 14.17. The exact charge Z/(i-beta), support transport, noetherian zero-charge torsion conclusion, and the separate Hom-vanishing refinement are implemented. CLOSEOUT REVIEW 2026-08-14: the type-two classification predicate stores phase-cut membership and the positive-new-imaginary Hom implication, whereas the printed Lemma 14.17 states Hom vanishing as a subsequent moreover conclusion. The current biconditional is therefore a strengthened candidate, not a literal source binding. Issue #208 and epic #192 remain open; this coordinate stays mapped and must not be promoted.

evidence.v4_check: Pages 71--74 were checked directly against the pinned v4 PDF. The display (14.1) cutoff conventions, Definition 14.12 envelope, and Proposition 14.16 charge normalization match the source-facing adapters. Lemma 14.17 does not yet have a literal biconditional because the Lean type-two predicate includes an additional Hom-vanishing implication. The mapped status records this candidate and explicit mismatch; it is not a reviewed coverage claim.

near_term_coordinates.note: Uniform quadratic support across a family. PROMOTED target -> mapped 2026-08-11: Support/Quadratic.lean supplies a genuine bundled QuadraticForm and its implication to the norm support predicate; Support/Uniform.lean forces one form across an indexed family and supplies constant-family, reindexing, union-locus, and linear-equivalence transport; Support/ZeroChargeLattice.lean constructs the saturated subgroup generated by zero classes and proves its finite quotient free abelian; Support/Quotient.lean puts the descended charge and one uniform form on the real quotient; Weak/Support/Quadratic.lean binds these predicates to actual nonzero weak-semistable heart classes and stores charge compatibility. UPDATE 2026-08-15: Support/Semistable.lean binds the ordinary locus to classes of nonzero objects in an actual slicing phase and supplies fixed-category uniform packages under #380. Support/IntegralRealQuotient.lean now constructs the canonical map from the saturated integral quotient, its real scalar extension, the formula on original classes, and an equivalence exactly under an explicit bijectivity proof (#387). This remains a fixed-category numerical candidate: the comparison's bijectivity is model-specific, and varying geometric fibers, HN structures, boundedness, and moduli functors remain explicit boundaries. The coordinate is therefore not reviewed or formalized.

evidence.v4_check: Read directly from the pinned v4 PDF on 2026-08-11. Page 87: Definition 18.5 fixes a Mukai homomorphism and says a (weak) HN structure satisfies support with respect to a quadratic form Q when its torsion-heart stability data does; Lemma 18.6 identifies this with the same Q on every fiber. Page 101: Definition 21.9 forms the saturated zero-class subgroup Lambda_0 and the free quotient Lambda/Lambda_0. Page 102: Definition 21.15(4) places Q on the real quotient, requires negativity on the descended kernel and nonnegativity on every fiber semistable class; clause (5) is boundedness and remains outside this mapping.

near_term_coordinates.note: TARGET UPDATED 2026-08-11: Families/Basic.lean isolates candidate interfaces for universally locally constant charge, universal openness, weak generic openness, ordinary and weak HN integration after caller-designated Dedekind base changes, and boundedness. Families/Ordinary.lean combines Definition 20.5(1)-(3) with Definition 21.15(4)-(5), using the genuine quotient-uniform support predicate, and supplies a fully inhabited PUnit constant-family witness. Families/Weak.lean binds clause (0), charges, semistability loci, and quotient support to actual indexed weak stability functions on one fixed category and heart, again with an inhabited PUnit witness. Families/Theorem22.lean records the four source clauses used by Theorem 22.2 and every currently missing geometric dependency. Candidate declaration/source-coordinate links now exist, but governance keeps this coordinate at target pending adversarial review and owner acceptance; a later mapped status would still be only a candidate mapping, not a source-faithfulness verdict. The repository still has no schemes, varying fiber categories, base-change functors, relative hearts, moduli spaces, bounded-family constructions, complex-manifold structures, proof of Theorem 22.2, or implementation of the later Section 23 results.
